I am 50 this year, and I have been farming my 13.1 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. All my land is cotton. Last year I planted the improved Bt cotton variety that I bought from the seed dealer in town. For each mu I put down one full bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as base — that is 50 jin — and then I top-dressed twice with urea, 20 jin at first flowering and another 15 jin when the bolls were setting. The dealer told me that 15-15-15 means 7.5 jin of real nitrogen per bag, and urea is 46% nitrogen, so I figure that is about 24 kg of nitrogen per mu all together. I also got 7.5 kg of phosphorus and potassium from the compound. I turned the soil once with the rotary tiller before planting, irrigated three times from my well, and sprayed pesticide four times. My yield was around 310 kg per mu.

This year I will do the same thing. My neighbor Lao Zhang used the exact same variety and fertilizer last year and got 330 kg per mu, so I know this works. Fertilizer prices went up a little, but I am not cutting back. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. Besides, my son and daughter-in-law both work in the Handan factory and send money home, so I have cash to buy inputs. I would rather spend the money now than regret it in autumn. I will rotary till once in late April, plant the improved Bt cotton, put down the base fertilizer, and then follow the same top-dress schedule. I will irrigate at planting, at flowering in July, and at boll stage in August. I will spray four times: once for aphids when the seedlings are small, and then for spider mites and whitefly later. I may hire two or three people to help pick in October if the bolls are heavy. If the weather cooperates, I expect 330 kg per mu.
